output.title: Attribution starts with one source field you can trust
output.body:
If you are measuring attribution, the first decision is not which dashboard to buy. It is whether your leads already pass through one place where the source can be recorded in a way you can trust. If the answer is no, attribution is a data-plumbing problem, not an AI problem.

For a small business, that usually means checking one workflow: website form, email reply, CRM entry, or sales record. Ask a simple question: when a lead becomes a customer, can you trace it back to one channel or campaign without guessing? If the answer depends on memory, a spreadsheet note, or whatever someone typed last Tuesday, the measurement is already shaky.

A practical next step is a small manual spot-check. Pick a short recent set of closed deals, look up the true source from the original trail, and compare it with what your CRM or tracking field says. You are not trying to prove the whole system works from one sample; you are checking whether the control is real or just decorative. Small businesses love decorative controls right up until they need them.

If the source field is blank, inconsistent, or routinely overwritten, fix the input rule before adding AI. Once source data is reliable, then you can decide whether lead scoring, channel-based replies, or another automation is worth testing. Before that, the model would just be helping you measure noise more neatly.
